issue.title: Next build can’t resolve `.tsx` files via `.js` imports with package `type` as `"module"`

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue was opened via the bug report template.

issue.body:
### Verify canary release

- [X] I verified that the issue exists in the latest Next.js canary release

### Provide environment information

Operating System:
      Platform: darwin
      Arch: arm64
      Version: Darwin Kernel Version 21.6.0: Thu Sep 29 20:13:56 PDT 2022; root:xnu-8020.240.7~1/RELEASE_ARM64_T6000
    Binaries:
      Node: 19.0.0
      npm: 8.19.2
      Yarn: 1.22.19
      pnpm: N/A
    Relevant packages:
      next: 13.0.3-canary.2
      eslint-config-next: N/A
      react: 18.2.0
      react-dom: 18.2.0

### What browser are you using? (if relevant)

N/A

### How are you deploying your application? (if relevant)

N/A

### Describe the Bug

When the Next.js project `package.json` file has the `type` field set to `"module"`, and you have `tsconfig.json` configured with `compilerOptions.moduleResolution` set to `"nodenext"`, and within a page component module you attempt to import another `.tsx` module (e.g. a component from a `components` directory) via an import path with the `.js` file extension, when running `next build` there is a Webpack build error that the module was not found and can't be resolved. This is incorrect; TypeScript is able to resolve the module just fine when looking at the import in VS Code with intelligence or when checking the project with `tsc --noEmit`.

### Expected Behavior

Next.js should be able to build project TypeScript modules that import `.tsx` files via an import path with the `.js` file extension without error.

### Link to reproduction - Issues with a link to complete (but minimal) reproduction code will be addressed faster

N/A

### To Reproduce

In `package.json`:

```json
{
  "name": "next-bug-demo",
  "private": true,
  "type": "module",
  "scripts": {
    "dev": "next dev",
    "build": "next build",
    "start": "next start",
    "type-check": "tsc --noEmit"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "@types/node": "18.11.9",
    "@types/react": "18.0.25",
    "@types/react-dom": "18.0.8",
    "next": "^13.0.3-canary.2",
    "react": "18.2.0",
    "react-dom": "18.2.0"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "typescript": "^4.8.4"
  }
}
```

In `tsconfig.json`:

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "es5",
    "lib": ["dom", "dom.iterable", "esnext"],
    "allowJs": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "strict": true,
    "forceConsistentCasingInFileNames": true,
    "noEmit": true,
    "esModuleInterop": true,
    "module": "esnext",
    "moduleResolution": "nodenext",
    "resolveJsonModule": true,
    "isolatedModules": true,
    "jsx": "preserve",
    "incremental": true
  },
  "include": ["**/.*", "**/*"],
  "exclude": ["node_modules"]
}
```

Note that this is not my desired TypeScript config; Next.js overwrites the config with "mandatory" config every `next dev`. For example; ideally Next.js would respect a `compilerOptions.module` value of `nodenext`. I don't think this gripe is the source of the bug being reported in this issue though, since TypeScript with the same config resolves ok the imports Next.js fails to resolve at build.

In `pages/index.tsx`:

```tsx
import Demo from "../Demo.js";

export default function Home() {
  return <Demo />;
}
```

In `Demo.tsx`:

```tsx
export default function Demo() {
  return <>Demo.</>;
}
```

Run `npm run build` and notice this build error:

```
> build
> next build

info  - Linting and checking validity of types  
info  - Creating an optimized production build  
Failed to compile.

./pages/index.tsx
Module not found: Can't resolve '../Demo.js' in '[redacted]/pages'


> Build failed because of webpack errors
```

Note that TypeScript is able to resolve the imports fine if you check the types with `npm run type-check`:

```

> type-check
> tsc --noEmit

```

body:
Not sure exactly why that's happening, but you could try reporting that over in https://github.com/webpack/webpack/issues/13252, since that's the related issue in the webpack repo.

If you find a solution, let us know and I'll update my post above.

Or you could try **Workaround 2**, which uses `webpack.NormalModuleReplacementPlugin` instead.

issue.title: allow voluntary .ts suffix for import paths

labels.name: Fix Available
labels.description: A PR has been opened for this issue

repository.name: TypeScript
repository.description: TypeScript is a superset of JavaScript that compiles to clean JavaScript output.

issue.body:
## Search Terms
.ts
suffix
imports
extension

## Suggestion
Typescript doesn't recognize file imports with ```.ts``` suffix.
Allow voluntary ```.ts``` to be added to import paths.
## Use Cases

It seems right to be able to use a correct path to a file without magic resolution.
This would help to align with [deno](https://deno.land) which uses mandatory suffixes o files.

## Examples

let
```import a from "path/to/a.ts"```
behave the same as 
```import a from "path/to/a"```

## Checklist

My suggestion meets these guidelines:

* [x] This wouldn't be a breaking change in existing TypeScript/JavaScript code
* [x] This wouldn't change the runtime behavior of existing JavaScript code
* [x] This could be implemented without emitting different JS based on the types of the expressions
* [x] This isn't a runtime feature (e.g. library functionality, non-ECMAScript syntax with JavaScript output, etc.)
* [x] This feature would agree with the rest of [TypeScript's Design Goals](https://github.com/Microsoft/TypeScript/wiki/TypeScript-Design-Goals).

issue.title: Add support for tsconfig 'nodenext' | 'node16'
issue.body:
## ESM: support module option for tsconfig.json 

- fixes #37525
- fixes #41961

With [TypeScript 4.7 providing ECMAScript Module Support](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-4-7/#ecmascript-module-support-in-node-js), we can now set this in our tsconfig.json file for the [module](https://www.typescriptlang.org/tsconfig#module) option.

Webpack added "extensionAlias" to solve importing ts files with .js extension -> https://github.com/webpack/enhanced-resolve/pull/351
